title: Attack Surface Reduction & Evidence Collector: VPC Segmentation, Firewall Patterns, mTLS Flow, RBAC v2 & SIEM Mapping
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures a compact, implementation-focused pattern set for reducing attack surface on Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem installations). It ties network segmentation, host-level firewall rules, mutual TLS flows, RBAC v2 expectations, and audit/evidence automation together with concrete SIEM export mappings. The goal: prescriptive checklist and minimal config snippets to accelerate compliance reviews and customer audits.

Context and assumptions:
- Target environment: customer-managed VPCs (AWS/GCP/Azure) and air-gapped on-prem cluster variants with a private control plane.
- Components considered: control plane endpoints, inference servers (GPU hosts), autoscaler/agents, metrics/exporter nodes, evidence-collector (lightweight agent), bastion/admin jump hosts.
- Threat model highlights: lateral movement from compromised workload, exposed control-plane ports, leaked credentials/tokens, weak RBAC allowing token replay, insufficient audit trail.

High-level pattern summary:
1) Zero-exposure control plane: control plane endpoints only reachable from customer admin CIDRs and dedicated private connections (VPC peering/PrivateLink/Private Service Connect). No public IPs on control-plane interfaces.
2) Micro-segmentation by role: separate subnets/SGs for inference-pool, runtime-cache, metric-store, admin-plane, evidence-collector. Explicit allow-only rules between minimal pairs.
3) Host firewalls + cloud SGs: defense-in-depth by asserting the same deny-by-default rules at both cloud security groups and host-level (iptables/nft/homed firewall).
4) mTLS for everything machine-to-machine: service mesh or lightweight mTLS (Envoy or mutual TLS using customer KMS-backed certs) between control plane, agents, and evidence-collector.
5) RBAC v2 minimal privileges: short-lived machine identities + role bindings scoped to cluster/route level. Remove wildcard permissions.
6) Audit-first evidence automation: structured audit events emitted to local buffer, forwarded to evidence-collector with attestations and pushed to SIEM; retention policy and integrity checksum included.

VPC and subnet layout (reference pattern):
- VPC: private-only (no IGW on inference subnets).
- Subnets:
  - subnet-admin (10.10.0.0/24): bastion, admin APIs, jumpboxes
  - subnet-control-plane (10.10.1.0/24): control plane endpoints, CA, cert-issuers
  - subnet-inference-pool (10.10.2.0/22): GPU hosts (runtime)
  - subnet-system (10.10.6.0/24): autoscaler, scheduler, evidence-collector
  - subnet-monitoring (10.10.7.0/24): metrics, log-forwarders (no inbound from inference pool)
- Route tables: inference-pool routes only to system subnet and control-plane via SGs & host firewalls; no default route to internet.

Minimal firewall rules (cloud SG + host-level parity) - allow-list examples:
- Admin CIDR -> subnet-admin: TCP 22, 443 (admin API), 8200 (vault)
- subnet-admin -> subnet-control-plane: TCP 443 (control API)
- control-plane -> subnet-system: TCP 8443 (agent registration), TCP 5671 (message queue)
- system -> inference-pool: TCP 10250 (kubelet-like), TCP 50051 (gRPC), TLS port ranges for model serving
- inference-pool -> system: TCP 80/443 (health + upload logs) but only to evidence-collector endpoint
- outbound to SIEM (log-forwarder) restricted to monitoring subnet on TLS 6514 or HTTPS to vendor endpoints via private egress gateway
- Deny: all inbound from inference-pool to admin/control-plane ports not explicitly listed

mTLS flow (recommended minimal posture):
1) Root CA (customer-managed, KMS-protected) stored in control-plane vault; short-lived leaf certs minted by control-plane CA via CSR approval + RBAC-bound request.
2) Each service (agent, inference runtime, evidence-collector) obtains a cert with SANs limited to instance-id and service role.
3) Mutual TLS handshake enforces client cert verification and OID checks for role claims.
4) Certificate rotation: automatic every 7 days by default for machine certs; revocation list distributed via control-plane and cached locally.
5) Optional: integrate with SPIFFE/SPIRE to standardize identity claims across clouds.

RBAC v2 (machine identity model) - recommendations and compact role matrix:
- Principle: grant least privilege, ephemeral tokens, narrow scope bindings.
- Role examples (names and minimal permission lists):
  - pd:admin (full admin) -> API:controlplane.* (used only via admin subnet & MFA)
  - pd:agent -> registration:create, registration:renew, status:post (scoped to agent-id)
  - pd:evidence-collector -> logs:read:local, logs:forward, audit:fetch, attestation:sign
  - pd:metrics-forwarder -> metrics:read, metrics:push:siem-endpoint
  - pd:runtime-worker -> model:load, model:serve, cache:read
- Binding recommendations:
  - Machine identities belong to a single role; avoid multiple roles unless strictly required.
  - Token lifetime <= 1h for agent bootstrap; use certs for long-lived machine auth.
  - Admin operations require pd:admin plus originating IP in admin CIDR and MFA verification.

Audit log schema (JSON line format) - minimal event fields:
- timestamp: RFC3339
- event_id: UUIDv4
- source_service: short name (control-plane|agent|evidence-collector|runtime)
- source_host: instance-id or host fqdn
- principal: {\"type\": \"machine|user\", \"id\": \"<subject-id>\", \"roles\": [\"pd:agent\"]}  <-- flatten as stringified JSON for log shipper
- action: short token (e.g., registration:start, cert:issue, model:serve:invoke)
- resource: resource-type + id (e.g., runtime/model:resnet50:v2)
- outcome: success|failure
- request_id: tracing id
- signature: base64-integrity-hash (optional signed attestation)

Example log line (single line JSON):
{"timestamp":"2025-01-20T22:14:03Z","event_id":"9b3d9c8a-1a7f-4a4b-9c3f-2a5e1d6f77c2","source_service":"evidence-collector","source_host":"ec-07c4e7","principal":"{\"type\":\"machine\",\"id\":\"agent-13\",\"roles\":[\"pd:agent\"]}","action":"logs:forward","resource":"host:ec-07c4e7","outcome":"success","request_id":"trace-0ab2","signature":"sha256:Z2VybWFu..."}

Evidence collector: design notes and guarantees:
- Lightweight footprint: single binary (Go) that reads local audit log files and the structured JSON stream (stdout) from services; performs local checksum and queues for upload.
- Integrity: each batch contains a Merkle root over events and a batch signature signed by the evidence-collector machine key.
- Tamper-evidence: evidence-collector keeps a write-once append-only file and periodically stamps blocks with signed checkpoint metadata pushed to SIEM and to a customer-specified S3/GCS bucket (with object immutability).
- Delivery modes: push (TLS to local log-forwarder) or pull (SIEM collector polls via authenticated endpoint).
- Backpressure safety: local disk spool with size quota and eviction policy; alerts to SRE if spool > 80% capacity.

SIEM export mapping (Elastic/Chronicle/Seq style):
- Transport: TLS 6514 (syslog over TLS) or HTTPS POST to ingestion API.
- Field mapping (source -> SIEM field):
  - timestamp -> @timestamp
  - event_id -> event.id
  - source_service -> host.service
  - source_host -> host.hostname
  - principal -> user.name (string) and user.roles (tag)
  - action -> event.action
  - resource -> resource.name
  - outcome -> event.outcome
  - request_id -> trace.id
  - signature -> event.hash
- Enrichment: add tags: {deployment_env, customer_id, region, cluster_id, evidence_batch_id}
- Alerts to create:
  - repeated auth failures from same principal within 5m -> high
  - evidence upload failed and spool growth > 50% -> medium
  - unexpected control-plane API calls from inference-pool -> critical

Hardening checklist (practical step-by-step, target audience: SRE/eng on private-deploy install)
- Pre-deploy (design):
  - [ ] Validate private subnet design with security team and require no IGW for inference subnets
  - [ ] Define admin CIDR and rotate allowed CIDRs with change control
  - [ ] Prepare root CA and CA rotation policy; ensure KMS-backed storage
- Networking & firewall:
  - [ ] Create cloud SGs for each subnet and mirror deny-by-default host firewall rules
  - [ ] Block direct internet egress from inference-pool; force egress through egress-gateway for updates only
  - [ ] Limit SIEM endpoints to monitoring subnet and apply TLS pinned certificates
- Identity & mTLS:
  - [ ] Install certificate issuer in control-plane and test CSR flow for agent certs
  - [ ] Enforce client-cert verification on all internal APIs; validate OID role claims
  - [ ] Set cert lifetime and test rotation/revocation paths
- RBAC & tokens:
  - [ ] Audit existing role bindings; remove wildcard rules and orphaned principals
  - [ ] Set token lifetimes, require short bootstrap token and cert-based machine auth
- Audit & evidence:
  - [ ] Deploy evidence-collector in system subnet; validate local spool, signature generation, and checkpointing
  - [ ] Configure SIEM export (TLS + mapped fields) and run end-to-end test with synthetic events
  - [ ] Enable immutable storage for evidence batches in S3/GCS with retention policy per customer contract
- Monitoring & runbook:
  - [ ] Add metrics and alerts for spool utilization, cert expiry < 48h, failed deliveries > 5 in 1h
  - [ ] Create incident runbook: evidence-collector failure -> failover to pull-mode -> open PD ticket -> notify customer contacts

Operational snippets and quick commands:
- Host firewall (example nftables rule to deny all then allow agent to evidence-collector):
  nft add table ip pd
  nft add chain ip pd input { type filter hook input priority 0; policy drop; }
  nft add rule ip pd input ip saddr 10.10.6.0/24 tcp dport 6514 accept
  nft add rule ip pd input ip saddr 10.10.2.0/22 tcp dport 50051 accept  # runtime -> system gRPC

- CSR flow (openssl minimal example):
  openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -out agent.key -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048
  openssl req -new -key agent.key -subj "/CN=agent-13/O=pd:agent" -out agent.csr
  # POST agent.csr to control-plane CSR endpoint over TLS with short bootstrap token

- Evidence batch verification (client-side verify command):
  evidence-collector verify --bundle /var/lib/evidence/batch-20250121.tar --ca /etc/pd/ca.pem --signer-key /etc/pd/collector.pub

Frequently asked questions (short):
Q: Can customers disable evidence-collector?
A: Evidence-collector is optional but recommended for compliance. If disabled, require centralized SIEM forwarder and extend attestation windows; document the additional customer responsibility in the SLO contract.

Q: How do we support air-gapped installs?
A: Use pull-mode: evidence-collector exposes an authenticated endpoint on the monitoring subnet; disconnected SIEM collectors periodically pull batches over an internal secure channel. Ensure hardware HSM or Vault runs locally for signing keys.

Next steps and open decisions:
- PoC integration with SPIFFE to reduce bespoke OID checks (owner: Diego Morales; JIRA-PD-298)
- Harden default certificate lifetime to 7 days and validate rotation tooling across cloud providers (owner: Rina Patel; due: 2025-02-18)
- Define minimal legal retention and cross-customer evidence isolation for multi-tenant dedicated racks (security review Q1 2025)

References and links:
- Confluence design doc (iteration): CONFLUENCE-PLANS-1423
- Implementation PR: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-evidence-collector/pull/56
- Related audit schema draft: CONFLUENCE-AUDIT-SCHEMA-V2

Appendix: informal diagram (ASCII) - show segmentation and flows:
  [Admin CIDR]
      |
  [subnet-admin] --(443)--> [control-plane subnet]
                              |  (cert minting)
                              v
                        [system subnet:evidence-collector] <--(TLS 6514)-- [monitoring subnet:siem-forwarder]
                              ^                                   
                              |(gRPC 50051)
                      [inference-pool runtime hosts]

End of document.
